newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran blasts German "interference" over journalist.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts German "interference" over journalist.

text.p: Iran criticised what it called German interference in the case of an Iranian journalist who was arrested while trying to leave the country this month, state-run Tehran Radio reported on Thursday.
It quoted foreign ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi as saying the arrest and trial of Faraj Sarkuhi was an internal affair and any foreign interference was "unacceptable."
"The arrest and trials of criminals including Sarkuhi is a common matter related to the internal affairs of Iran and any foreign interference in this matter is unacceptable," he said.
"We cannot be pressured by foreign political propaganda to disregard our principles and laws in the case of a person who has committed serious offences," Mohammadi added.
Bonn said on Tuesday its ambassador in Tehran was told Sarkuhi, the editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday) magazine, was arrested on Sunday while trying to leave the country illegally.

Iran's news agency IRNA on Thursday said Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati sent his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel a letter about the issue. The letter was handed to the German envoy to Tehran by ministry official Ali Ahani on Wednesday.

Germany had asked Iran for details of the whereabouts of Sarkuhi following reports last week he had not only been detained and tortured for 47 days last year when Iran said he was in Germany, but had now been arrested again.
A German foreign ministry spokesman said Bonn still wanted Iran to comment on these allegations, made in a letter from Sarkuhi which was published in several German newspapers.
The spokesman also said documents provided by Iran to prove Sarkuhi visited Germany last year -- when he says he was being tortured in detention -- were probably false.

In a Tehran news conference arranged by the authorities on Thursday, Sarkuhi's brother Esmaeil said he and Sarkuhi were arrested on Saturday near the Gulf port city of Bushehr while arranging for smugglers to get them out of the country by boat.
He said he had decided to help his brother leave the country because Sarkuhi was depressed and attempted suicide on several recent occasions.
He largely confirmed Iran's version of the events.
Esmaeil Sarkuhi said he had been released but his brother was still being held.

He said he had faxed his brother's letter abroad without reading it. Sarkuhi said in the letter, which Bonn believes is genuine, he had been held by the Iranian secret service and tortured into confessing in a taped interview that he had spied for Germany.

He said he believed Iran intends to use the confession in a row with Germany over an accusation by German prosecutors that Iranian leaders ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin in 1992.
An Iranian and four Lebanese are being tried for the killings. Iran denies any involvement.
